Finding: var is used pervasively across colors.js, details-panel.js,       
  expand-ui.js, graph-utils.js, icons.js, legend.js, renderers.js. Only      
  entity-types.js and legend-state.js use const/let. This produces           
  function-scoped bindings that hoist, allow accidental redeclaration (e.g.  
  var html declared twice in details-panel.js:49, 60 inside the same function
   — silent in var, an error with let), and signal pre-ES2015 style.         
  Fix: Replace var with const (default) or let (when reassigned). At the same
   time, switch function () callbacks to arrow functions where they don't    
  need their own this/arguments (e.g. all the .forEach(function (...) {}),   
  dataGraph.forEachNode(function (...) {}) callbacks). This also removes the
  need for the unused function keyword in inline iterators.                  
  Impact: Catches bugs at parse time, eliminates a class of hoisting/scope
  mistakes, and aligns the file with the rest of the codebase's modern
  subset.

Priority: High
  Finding: selection.js defines getOrInitNodeHidden, but LegendState.initNode
   (legend-state.js:36) now owns this responsibility. getOrInitNodeHidden    
  does not appear to be imported anywhere in src/rysiai/. It's dead code that
   drifts from the real implementation.                                      
  Fix: Verify there are no remaining importers (grep -r 
  "getOrInitNodeHidden\|selection.js" src test), then delete                 
  src/rysiai/selection.js.
  Impact: One less file to read, no risk of someone wiring up the stale      
  helper and bypassing LegendState's invariants.
